title: OSS LLM intake: deterministic conversion, compatibility mapping, and publishing performance signatures
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Ship an end-to-end, deterministic pipeline that takes community OSS LLM weights and produces a Redwood-ready model artifact, a stable version pin, and a published performance signature (latency/cost/quality) suitable for runtime routing and customer guidance. Scope: weights ingestion (manifest v2), deterministic conversion to canonical runtime format, quantization candidate generation, runtime compatibility mapping (kernel and memory footprint), automated smoke and regression tests, and performance signature publishing into the model catalog. Out of scope: long-tail model family-specific optimizations and live user-facing catalog UI changes (handled in a follow-up story).
acceptance_criteria: A standardized manifest (manifest-v2) is accepted by the intake API and stored in the artifact bucket with provenance metadata and signed checksums.
A deterministic converter run (safepath-convert v2) produces bit-stable runtime artifacts across two independent runs on identical inputs.

The pipeline emits a performance signature: median p95 token latency for standard prompt set, cost estimate per 1k tokens for each quantization candidate, and a quality delta score vs baseline on our eval suite.
A canary release path publishes the pinned model to staging catalog and triggers runtime smoke tests in dedicated staging cluster. Failures create automated rollbacks and detailed incident artifacts.
Telemetry is emitted for every stage: ingest, convert, validate, profile, and publish for post-mortem and SLO tracking.
engineering_notes: 2026-02-19: Initial spike completed. Evaluated existing conversion tools (torch-ckpt -> runtime canonical) and found nondeterministic ordering in state_dict keys for community checkpoints. Decided to normalize with stable manifest ordering and hash-sorted tensors before conversion.

2026-02-25: Design decision: use safetensors as canonical on-disk interchange format where possible to avoid PyTorch pickling variability. Fallback to deterministic Torch save with explicit key ordering for legacy checkpoints.

2026-03-02: Implemented conversion harness prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-converter/pull/47 (link). Prototype demonstrates identical output hashes across two runs on identical inputs in CI (see artifact hashes in PR).

2026-03-05: Performance profiling harness added. Runs a standard prompt corpus (20 prompts, mixture of short/long) to measure p50/p95 latency and token throughput. Stores results as 'performance-signature-v1' in the catalog. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/12 (link).

2026-03-08: Quantization candidates generation: float16, dynamic-8bit, and GPTQ-4bit configured. Trade-off: GPTQ gives best memory reduction but requires additional verification time (~30% longer profile run). Chosen default: float16 and GPTQ candidate for medium/large models; dynamic-8bit for <7B models.

2026-03-10: Runtime compatibility mapping implemented: kernel profile mapping table produced for A100-40GB and T4-16GB. Will extend to L40 and V100 next cycle. Mapping includes expected peak memory, preferred kernels, and fallback kernels for short/long sequence workloads.

2026-03-11: Canary plan: stage pin to staging-catalog with tag 'canary-ENG-725432', run 3 smoke iterations (success criteria: zero fatal errors, p95 within 1.25x of baseline, deterministic outputs for static prompt set). If any failure, auto-rollback and create ENG-725432-rollback report.
Next steps: finalize manifest-v2 docs (Confluence), wire S3 lifecycle and signed manifest storage, and get security review sign-off for safetensors handling and KMS integration.
